description: Reviewed per-capita and share pairings (ADR-0009). Only an entry with status `approved` is served; `draft` entries are proposals awaiting the owner's review. An ACS entry's `{dataset}` placeholder expands to each listed dataset, as `<ratio_id>:<dataset>`. A `provider_rate` entry names the rate the provider publishes for its count; nothing is recomputed beside it. An `agency_rate` entry (ADR-0012) is a county crime rate computed in gold from FBI agency reports: the reporting agencies' offenses over their own FBI populations, beside the FBI rate it names in `reads_beside`. A `time_cost` entry (ADR-0009 amendment, 2026-11-06) is minutes of work: a BLS average price divided by the QCEW average weekly wage over `hours_per_week`; its `{area}` placeholder expands to each listed BLS area code, as `<ratio_id>:<area>`, and the reader names the wage's area. A county childcare price (`DOL_CHILDCARE`) names no area: it is the county's own, divided by that county's wage.

entries.label: Median property tax as a percent of median home value
entries.rationale: Both medians describe the same owner-occupied homes in the same ACS dataset, release and period, so their ratio is the Bureau's derived ratio of two estimates (ADR-0009 rules 2 and 4). The taxes are not a part of the value, so it is a ratio, not a share. Named in deliverable T-2 of the taxes-and-public-money plan, which Nick approved as option B on 2026-11-05.
limitations: A ratio of two medians, not the median of each home's own tax rate: the homes paying the median tax need not be the homes of median value.
Survey estimate: the margin of error is the Census Bureau's approximation for a derived ratio, at 90 percent confidence, and is wider than either input's relative error suggests for small places.
Home value is the owner's own estimate; where values have risen faster than assessments, the ratio falls without any change in tax law.
Numerator and denominator come from the same ACS dataset, release and period; a 5-year ratio describes the five-year period, not its last year.

entries.unit: per 100,000 people covered by reporting agencies in this county
entries.label: Violent crime per 100,000 people, computed from agency reports
entries.denominator_label: FBI population of the agencies serving only this county that reported
entries.universe: people covered by the reporting agencies that serve only this county
entries.rationale: ADR-0012, accepted with this pairing by Nick on 2026-10-31 (50 % coverage floor, coverage shown beside the figure): violent offenses reported by the agencies serving only this county, divided by those agencies' FBI-published populations, the way the FBI computes a state rate. Both sides are FBI figures from one release and one month, so ADR-0009 rule 2 holds. Version 2 (2026-10-31) reads the agencies from the FBI's Return A master file, which holds every agency, instead of the CDE's six-agency sample; the method is unchanged.
limitations: Agencies serving more than one county, and agencies with no published population, are left out of both sides.
The rate describes the people its reporting agencies cover, not every county resident: where a sheriff and town police both serve a county, each agency's population is its own jurisdiction's.
No rate is shown when no agency reported, when only multi-county agencies reported, or when the reporting agencies cover under half the population the county's agencies serve.
Monthly, like the agency reports it divides; never rolled up into a year. Not comparable with a Census per-capita figure.

entries.label: Share of personal income from all payments from government and others
entries.rationale: Transfer receipts are a component of personal income (CAINC4 line 47), so the program's receipts over personal income is the share of residents' income the program provides. Both figures are BEA's, for the same county, year and release (ADR-0009 rule 2).
limitations: Payments respond to a place's age and income; a high share describes who lives there, it does not cause it.
Medical benefits count as income of the people whose care they pay for.

BEA publishes the county program detail about a year after the county totals; a year whose CAINC35 and CAINC1 releases differ has no share on /observations/derived and says so (different_period); the /public-money payments card pairs the two county files by year and names both releases.

entries.label: Minutes of work to buy a dozen eggs, grade A large
entries.denominator_label: the average weekly wage of all jobs located in the wage's area (QCEW, all industries, all ownerships), over a 40-hour week
entries.universe: an hour of the average job located in the wage's area
entries.rationale: Nick approved minutes of work on 2026-11-06 as the relatable reading of an everyday price. BLS publishes the average price for the nation and the four Census regions only; QCEW publishes the average weekly wage for counties, states and the nation. The price's area and the wage's area are both named beside every value.
limitations: The price is the Census region's urban average (or the nation's); the wage is the reader's own county, state or nation, so the two areas differ and both are named.
The QCEW average weekly wage is total wages over jobs located in the area, by employer, including part-time jobs; 40 hours is an assumed week, not a measured one.
The price is one month's; the wage is that calendar year's annual average, or the newest year QCEW has published when the price's year has none yet, and the row says so.

entries.label: Share of households with one or more people under 18
entries.rationale: B11005_002 counts a subset of the households B11005_001 counts, in the same ACS table, release and period; the share is the Bureau's derived proportion of the two (ADR-0009 rules 2-4). Named in the starting-a-family-collection plan, which Nick approved on 2026-11-10.
limitations: Survey estimate: the margin of error is the Census Bureau's approximation for a derived proportion, at 90 percent confidence, and is wider than either input's relative error suggests for small places.
Counts households with any person under 18, including grandchildren and other relatives, not only the householder's own children.
Numerator and denominator come from the same ACS dataset, release and period; a 5-year share describes the five-year period, not its last year.

entries.label: Public school students per full-time-equivalent teacher
entries.denominator_label: full-time-equivalent teachers in the same public schools
entries.universe: public schools NCES places in the county or state
entries.rationale: Both are NCES Common Core of Data sums over the same placed schools for the same school year (ADR-0009 rule 2). Students are not a part of teachers, so it is a ratio. Divided only where every placed school reported both, because a partial sum over a partial sum describes neither the place nor its schools. Named in the starting-a-family-collection plan, which Nick approved on 2026-11-10.
limitations: A ratio of two sums over the place's public schools, not the size of any class: teachers include those who teach no regular class, and the count is full-time-equivalent.
Served only where both sums are complete; a place with any school not reporting either figure has no value (partial_input).
Public schools only; private schools are not counted. Labelled with the school year's fall: 2024 is 2024-25.
NCES publishes membership and staff as separate files for each school year, so the two sides of a year are different releases; each row names both.

entries.label: Minutes of work to pay one month's Fair Market Rent for a three-bedroom home
entries.denominator_label: the average weekly wage of all jobs located in the county (QCEW, all industries, all ownerships), over a 40-hour week
entries.universe: an hour of the average job located in the county
entries.rationale: Nick approved hours of work for the three-bedroom Fair Market Rent on 2026-11-10 ("Yes show hours of work"), with the dollar rent shown first and the calculation stated beside it, as for childcare. HUD sets the rent for the county's HUD area and repeats it for each county in it; the wage is the county's own QCEW average weekly wage.
limitations: The rent is the HUD area's (a metro area, a HUD metro subdivision or a nonmetropolitan county); the wage is the county's own, so where the area spans several counties each reads the same rent over its own wage, and both are named.
The QCEW average weekly wage is total wages over jobs located in the county, by employer, including part-time jobs; 40 hours is an assumed week, not a measured one.

The rent's year is HUD's fiscal year, which starts on October 1 of the year before, matched to the wage of that calendar year; for a rent newer than QCEW's newest year the newest wage is used and the row says which year.
